examples.name: Sample — an organisation chart
paragraphs: A staffing chart: boxed roles connected by rules into a strict hierarchy, five departments across the top and two separate contracted-services blocks below.

This is the case Mermaid is for. The content is entirely nodes and edges — who reports to whom — and none of the meaning lives in where a box sits on the page. Redrawn by a layout engine it would still say the same thing, which is exactly the test that a circuit or a floor plan fails.

Two things are easy to lose and MUST be carried across: the numbered suffixes distinguishing repeated roles (事務員①, 事務員②), and the annotations inside or beside the boxes (週29H, 週1×4H) — those are hours, not decoration, and they belong to the node they sit with. Each bracketed department label (＜管理課＞) names the group above it and becomes a subgraph title. Edges follow the printed rules: each department head connects by a rule to the stack of roles beneath it. The two lower blocks print no connecting rules, so their roles are grouped without edges. Expected boxes: the title line, and the chart as one Picture box.

[Images and Figures](12-images-and-diagrams-1-images-images-and-figures.html)§12.1.2 — how every other kind of figure is rendered - [Slide Diagrams](12-images-and-diagrams-2-diagrams-slide-diagrams.html)§12.2.5 — the `diagram` block for labelled figures that are not graphs - [Electrical Schematics](12-images-and-diagrams-2-diagrams-electrical-schematics.html)§12.2.3 — a graph-looking figure that Mermaid would misrepresent - [Blueprints](12-images-and-diagrams-2-diagrams-blueprints.html)§12.2.1 — spatial content with no graph in it - [Geographic Maps](12-images-and-diagrams-2-diagrams-geographic-maps.html)§12.2.4 — geography that a layout engine would discard Skill text for this ruleGenerator skill- When a figure is a graph (flowchart, organisation chart, process with arrows), render it as a ```mermaid flowchart: one node per box with its full printed text, one edge per printed connector or arrow, edge labels as printed. - Keep numbered suffixes (①, ②), hours and other annotations printed with a box inside that node's label; use a subgraph titled with a printed group label. - Do not draw edges the page does not print. - If the figure is really a table, use an HTML ; if position or orientation carries meaning (circuit, floor plan, map, molecule), do not use Mermaid. - Never leave a diagram out.Checker skill- FAIL (MUST) if a diagram printed on the page has no rendering at all in the Markdown. - FAIL (MUST) if a box label, numbered suffix or annotation printed in a graph-shaped diagram is missing from the rendering. - FAIL (MUST) if a circuit, floor plan, map or structural formula is rendered as a Mermaid graph. - FAIL (MUST) if a graph-shaped diagram (nodes joined by lines or arrows) is rendered as prose or a diagram block instead of a mermaid block. - WARN (SHOULD) if the Mermaid edges do not match the connectors printed on the page.
